summary:
Design B: an optional local answerability model. A QNLI cross-encoder (cross-encoder/qnli-electra-base, Apache-2.0, the publisher's own int8 ONNX export, 111 MB) scores each (question, source) pair for the top-5 context sources, in rank order, using context['scores'][id]['rank'] from the shipped rag.py interface. Passages are formatted as '<speaker>: <content>', with the date and the 'Summary:' line removed. For counting and date-arithmetic questions it also scores one evidence-seeking paraphrase ('how many cities...' becomes 'which cities...'; 'how many months after...' becomes 'when...'). A speaker-attribution filter applies when the question names a speaker found in the context: then only sources by that person or mentioning them count. The extractive generator abstains when the best counted QNLI logit is below -5.75. That threshold was tuned only on the dev calibration set plus the benchmark dev split (128 answerable, 52 unanswerable). The module is new (main/retrieval/answerability.py). It loads lazily, needs only onnxruntime, tokenizers and huggingface_hub, and is opt-in through generation.answer(..., answerability=True or a checker). The CLI flag is --answerability and the ablation flags are --answerability and --answerability-threshold. If the model is missing or fails, the answer is produced exactly as before and result['answerability']['status'] says 'unavailable'. The default None leaves output byte-identical.

Results after the freeze, run once: benchmark test 97.2% accepted, 52.2% refused, 74.7% balanced (no abstention 50.0, F6 55.9, template prior 56.3). LongMemEval 78.5 / 33.3 / 55.9 (no abstention 50.0, F6 54.0, template prior 62.2). LoCoMo 76.1 / 36.3 / 56.2 (no abstention 50.0, F6 49.1, template prior 49.3).

Verdict under the adoption rule: OPT-IN ONLY. It beats no abstention by 5.9 points on LongMemEval and 6.2 on LoCoMo, and it is better than no abstention, F6 and the template prior on the benchmark test split and on LoCoMo. But answerable acceptance on both external sets (78.5% and 76.1%) is far below the 90% gate. Most of those refusals happen when retrieval did not bring the evidence into context. Where the gold answer string is in a context source, the design refuses only 11 of 150 LongMemEval and 18 of 326 LoCoMo answerables. On LongMemEval the template prior has the higher balanced accuracy (62.2) but accepts only 51.1% of answerables. The latency budget (P50 at most 150 ms added) is met on the benchmark (74 to 105 ms) and on LoCoMo (136 to 157 ms, borderline). It is not met on LongMemEval (229 to 256 ms P50): long user turns plus a paraphrase on 30% of questions double the model calls. All latency was measured with load average around 7 to 8 from a concurrent measurement job, so it is likely pessimistic.

proposed_changes.description: New module, about 215 lines. OnnxQnliScorer loads the model lazily with onnxruntime + tokenizers. The weights come via huggingface_hub, local cache first; the cache dir is COGNIMEM_ANSWERABILITY_CACHE or data/rag/models, and the file is model_qint8_arm64.onnx on arm64 or model_quint8_avx2.onnx otherwise. Scoring takes logit[:,0], max_length 256, truncation only_second, and rejects NaN/inf output. Also adds passage_text(), question_variants() (counting and date-arithmetic paraphrase rewrites), attributable() (named-speaker filter; role speakers like 'user' are ignored), AnswerabilityChecker.assess(context), which never raises on model errors and returns status applied or unavailable, and default_checker(). DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=-5.75, DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCES=5. The full text is in the patch, lines 143-360.

proposed_changes.description: Adds an opt-in answerability parameter to answer(). It applies to the extractive generator only and is ignored by Gemini. The default None leaves behaviour unchanged.
proposed_changes.unified_diff:
@@ -80,11 +80,39 @@ def gemini_client(*, env_file='.env'):
-def answer(context, *, generator='gemini', client=None, env_file='.env'):
+def _answerability_checker(answerability):
+    if answerability is None or answerability is False:
+        return None
+    from .answerability import AnswerabilityChecker, default_checker
+    if answerability is True:
+        return default_checker()
+    if isinstance(answerability, AnswerabilityChecker):
+        return answerability
+    raise ValueError('answerability must be None, a bool, or an AnswerabilityChecker')
+
+
+def answer(context, *, generator='gemini', client=None, env_file='.env', answerability=None):
+    """...(docstring)..."""
     if generator not in {'gemini', 'extractive'}:
         raise ValueError('Unknown answer generator')
+    checker = _answerability_checker(answerability)
     if not context['sources']:
         return {'answer': 'Insufficient memory evidence.', 'abstain': True, 'statements': [], 'sources': {}, 'generator': generator}
+    if generator == 'extractive' and checker is not None:
+        assessment = checker.assess(context)
+        if not assessment['answerable']:
+            return {'answer': 'Insufficient memory evidence.', 'abstain': True, 'reason': 'not_answerable',
+                    'statements': [], 'sources': {}, 'generator': generator, 'answerability': assessment}
+        result = answer(context, generator=generator, client=client, env_file=env_file)
+        result['answerability'] = assessment
+        return result

proposed_changes.description: Adds Protocol.answerability (bool) and answerability_threshold. answer_extractive forwards a checker only when one is given, and build_answerability(protocol) returns a checker or None.
proposed_changes.unified_diff:
@@ -30,6 +30,8 @@ class Protocol:
     abstain_threshold: float | None = None
+    answerability: bool = False
+    answerability_threshold: float | None = None
@@ -50,11 +52,21 @@
-def answer_extractive(context: dict, threshold: float | None) -> dict:
+def answer_extractive(context: dict, threshold: float | None, answerability=None) -> dict:
     from main.retrieval.generation import answer
+    options = {} if answerability is None else {'answerability': answerability}
     if threshold is None:
-        return answer(context, generator='extractive')
-    return answer(context, generator='extractive', abstain_threshold=threshold)
+        return answer(context, generator='extractive', **options)
+    return answer(context, generator='extractive', abstain_threshold=threshold, **options)
+
+def build_answerability(protocol: Protocol):
+    if not protocol.answerability:
+        return None
+    from main.retrieval.answerability import DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, AnswerabilityChecker
+    threshold = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD if protocol.answerability_threshold is None else protocol.answerability_threshold
+    return AnswerabilityChecker(threshold=threshold)

dev_results:
Tuning data was only the dev calibration set (90 rows) and the benchmark dev split (90 rows, with the author's new unanswerables), on saved hybrid_full pool-20 top-5 contexts.

Model screen on the tuning data (AUROC of the max over top-5 sources, then LOPO balanced accuracy at 95% acceptance):
- qnli-electra-base: AUROC 0.899, LOPO 0.684
- nli-deberta-v3-xsmall (entail): 0.843, 0.550
- roberta-base-squad2 best-span: 0.866, 0.621
- qnli-distilroberta: 0.808, 0.561
- tinyroberta-squad2 best-span: 0.790, 0.580
- nli-MiniLM2: 0.757, 0.557
- mobilebert-squad2: 0.761, 0.523
- the existing reranker logit (baseline): 0.712, 0.546

SQuAD2 no-answer heads were near chance as answerability signals (AUROC 0.53 to 0.66). qnli-electra was chosen, with speaker-prefixed passages, the computed-question paraphrase and attribution. The threshold of -5.75 sits in the middle of the plateau where acceptance is 97.7%, which spans [-6.25, -5.46).

At the frozen threshold:
- Calibration set (45 answerable / 45 unanswerable): 95.6% accepted (43/45), 62.2% refused (28/45), 78.9% balanced, abstention precision 93.3%. Baselines: F6 80.0 / 11.1 / 45.6; template prior 44.4 / 22.2 / 33.3.
- Benchmark dev (83 / 7): 98.8% accepted (82/83), 85.7% refused (6/7), 92.3% balanced, precision 85.7%, grounded 95.6%. Baselines: F6 100 / 28.6 / 64.3; template prior 95.2 / 42.9 / 69.0.
final_heldout_check:
The design was frozen at 2026-10-11T22:14:30Z. sha256 of all 7 changed files plus the ONNX model and tokenizer are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephremingstonl-Downloads-code-capstone/2d91e859-4acd-4fbf-99c1-146f2e2aa197/scratchpad/f6rework/answerability-model/FROZEN_hashes.txt, re-verified OK before the external run. Held-out numbers were computed once each.

Benchmark test: evaluation.ablation --split test --candidate-limit 20 --answerability, run directory runs/HELDOUT_test_pool20_answerability. Also replayed on saved contexts, which gives the same numbers: runs/heldout_eval.log.
- 270 queries: 247 answerable, 23 unanswerable.
- This design: 97.2% accepted (240/247), 52.2% refused (12/23), 74.7% balanced, abstention precision 63.2%, grounded 91.5%.
- No abstention: 50.0% balanced, grounded 89.3%.

LongMemEval oracle: user turns as memories, *_abs questions should refuse; 500 rows, 470 answerable / 30 unanswerable. Output in work/eval_heldout_ext.json and runs/heldout_ext.log.
- This design: 78.5% accepted (369/470), 33.3% refused (10/30), 55.9% balanced, precision 9.0% (base rate 6.0%), grounded 29.8% (no abstention 30.0%).

LoCoMo: category 5 should refuse; 1986 rows, 1540 answerable / 446 unanswerable.
- This design: 76.1% accepted (1172/1540), 36.3% refused (162/446), 56.2% balanced, precision 30.6% (base rate 22.5%), grounded 23.7% (no abstention 16.4%).

Adoption rule:
- Benchmark acceptance of 97.2% passes the 95% gate.
- External acceptance fails the 90% gate on both sets (78.5% and 76.1%).
- Balanced accuracy beats no abstention by at least 3 points on both externals (+5.9 and +6.2).
- So it ships as opt-in only, not default-on. It is not worse than no abstention on any held-out set.

Post-freeze diagnosis, for reporting only and not used for tuning: most external refusals of answerables happen when the evidence is not in context. Where the gold answer string is in a context source, it refuses 11/150 on LongMemEval (92.7% conditional acceptance) and 18/326 on LoCoMo (94.5%). LongMemEval refusals cluster in single-session-assistant (30/56; the answer is in assistant turns, which are not stored as memories) and temporal-reasoning (46/133).

latency:
This is added latency per ask (AnswerabilityChecker.assess on up to 5 sources, 2 intra-op threads, int8 ONNX on arm64), measured with load average around 7 to 8 because a concurrent measure_all job was running.
- Benchmark test contexts: P50 73.7 ms, P95 104.1 ms (810 asks).
- Benchmark dev + calibration: P50 104.7 ms, P95 188.5 ms (540 asks).
- LoCoMo: P50 135.8 to 156.8 ms, P95 213.7 to 254.2 ms (400 to 1986 asks).
- LongMemEval: P50 228.7 to 255.6 ms, P95 528 to 601 ms (250 to 500 asks).
- Cold model load is 172 to 276 ms, once per process, plus a one-time download of about 111 MB.

The 150 ms P50 budget is met on the benchmark and is borderline on LoCoMo. It is missed on LongMemEval: user turns there are long (truncated at 256 tokens), and 30% of its questions get a second, paraphrased pass. Passing max_sources=3 or dropping the paraphrase would cut cost, but that was not measured, to keep the freeze intact.
tests:
Full suite in the repo copy (python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider) with COGNIMEM_ANSWERABILITY_CACHE pointing at the scratch model cache: 182 passed, 136 subtests passed, 1 unrelated collection warning. The known flake in tests/test_conversation_task_extensions.py did not appear.

Without the cache variable, tests/test_answerability.py gives 11 passed and 1 skipped (the real-model test). Nothing was downloaded, and data/rag/models in the main repo still holds only the bge and ms-marco models.

Other checks:
- evaluation.build_dataset --check passes with the author's seeds and gold_queries.json (456 memories, 360 queries, dev 90 / test 270).
- The patch applies cleanly to a fresh copy of the snapshot (git apply --check) and reproduces the 7 changed files byte for byte.
- The patch does not include the author's seed and gold_queries.json changes; those come from the author output.
risks:
1. External acceptance is below the gate (78.5% and 76.1%), so it must stay opt-in. It refuses many answerables when retrieval missed the evidence, and on aggregation and temporal questions whose answer is never stated in one sentence. That is defensible for grounding but costly for recall-oriented users.

2. On LongMemEval the template prior has the higher balanced accuracy (62.2 vs 55.9). It gets there by refusing half of all answerables, and on the external sets abstention precision stays low (9% and 31%).

3. The external latency P50 exceeds 150 ms on LongMemEval.

4. Tuning data is small (52 unanswerables) and written by an AI. The calibration set shares memories with the benchmark dev split, so the dev numbers are optimistic. The benchmark test unanswerable refusal of 52.2% rests on only 23 questions.

5. The attribution filter keys on first names that appear as speakers. Questions naming a non-speaker entity are unaffected, while a speaker name used generically could wrongly exclude evidence.

6. First use downloads about 111 MB from the HF hub into data/rag/models, unless COGNIMEM_ANSWERABILITY_CACHE is set. The model is English-only, and the int8 file is picked by architecture: arm64 gets qint8_arm64, everything else gets quint8_avx2, so a non-AVX2 x86 host could fail. That failure is caught as status 'unavailable' and the answer is produced as before.

7. Licences checked on the HF model cards: qnli-electra-base is Apache-2.0. SQuAD2 alternatives: tinyroberta-squad2 is CC-BY-4.0, while the onnx-community roberta-base and mobilebert exports state no licence on their cards.
confidence: High that the measurements are right and the protocol was followed: the threshold was tuned on dev data only, hashes were verified before the held-out run, and each held-out set was computed once. High that the verdict is opt-in only, because external acceptance misses the gate by more than 10 points. Moderate on how much it generalises: it beats no abstention by about 6 points on both externals and clearly beats F6 and the template prior on the benchmark test split and LoCoMo, but the evidence base is small and AI-authored.
root_cause: The F6 slot rule encoded the benchmark's two unanswerable templates, so it did not transfer to external data. A learned "does this sentence answer this question" signal (QNLI) separates answerable from unanswerable much better than the reranker logit: AUROC 0.899 vs 0.712 on tuning data. It generalises partly, gaining about 6 balanced points on both externals. But it cannot tell "the evidence is absent from memory" apart from "the evidence was not retrieved" or "the answer must be computed across sources". So at a threshold that keeps 97% benchmark acceptance, it refuses about a quarter of external answerables.
